topic: Macro Review 2026: Unified Open-Source System for Email, Chat, Tasks, Docs, and AI Agents
keyword: macro unified system email chat tasks docs agents

key_points: Macro is an all-in-one workspace combining email, messages, docs, tasks, code, agents, calls, and CRM into a single interface
Built with Rust backend and TypeScript/SolidJS frontend — AGPL-3.0 license, fully open source (not open core)
Raised $30M led by a16z, based in NYC — 689 GitHub stars, 134 forks as of July 2026
Key features: Unified Inbox, Unified Search, Unified Memory (nightly refresh), Bidirectional @linking, Channel-based permissions
MCP server available for AI agent integration — supports Claude Code, Codex, and any MCP client
SOC 2 Type II certified, ISO 27001 — zero data retention with model providers
Moved from BSL to AGPLv3 on May 31, 2026 — fully open source, not open core
Self-hostable under AGPLv3 terms; commercial licensing available separately
Pricing: same for personal and team plans; no free plan for teams
Comparison with Notion, Superhuman, Slack — Macro has purpose-built modules vs Notion's generic databases
Notion integration available via MCP connector for agents to access Notion data
Positioned as 'the open source workspace, one app for all your work'
Sign up with Google account, connect Gmail or Google Workspace
Built for speed in Rust and SolidJS — keyboard-first everywhere
Contribute, fork, extend and self-host messaging
Unified Memory: agents remember what the whole team is doing across email, messages, tasks, docs, and calls
Refreshed nightly from the day's activity — agents answer from most recent emails, messages, tasks, docs, and call transcripts
Personal memory vs team-level memory distinction
No need to manually point agents at context — it's automatically available
Migration guides available for Superhuman, Notion, Slack, Linear, and ClickUp
Notion Balkanization problem: teams start with Notion but eventually need best-in-class systems for each function
Macro positions as the unified alternative to the fragmented toolchain of separate apps
